LMP3.title: United inherit the LMP3 win after Duqueine’s pit-time penalty
LMP3.dek: Brundle, Guasch and England’s United Ligier #2 won a third race in three when Duqueine’s on-road victory, by 3.5 seconds, was reversed by a four-second penalty.

facts.v: Duqueine’s #19 crossed the line first but was given a four-second penalty for not respecting the minimum pit stop reference times, which dropped it behind the United #2.

chapters.title: United arrive with a perfect record
text: United Autosports came to Austria unbeaten: the #2 Ligier of Brundle, Guasch and England had won at both Silverstone and Imola. Bell, in the sister #3, expected the closest race so far and a strategic one, and practice bore him out. Boyd’s 1:26.146 in the #3 on Saturday morning was more than three tenths clear of Kaiser’s 360 Racing Ligier, and Gachet had led the class on Friday for Panis Barthez.

The paddock had shifted. Roda left Eurointernational, leaving Mondini and Jacoboni in the #11, while Rusinov stayed in the #12 as preparation for his World Endurance Championship weekend. Winslow took the Graff #9 in place of Guibbert and Maris returned to Oak’s #4 after the collapse of So24!. Murphy Prototypes was absent as its Ave-Riley AR-2 debut slipped again. The 19-year-old Jackson faced the longest stint of his career in the By Speed Factory #5, which ran only two drivers.

chapters.title: Gachet puts Panis Barthez on top
text: Gachet took LMP3 pole with a 1:26.126 in the #16, which he shares with Debard and Moineault. Five cars set the fastest time during the ten-minute session, which was red-flagged briefly when Maggi’s Race Performance #8 stopped at Turn 2. Boyd was 0.157s slower in the United #3 and Droux third in Duqueine’s #19.
Lahaye was fourth in Ultimate’s #17 and Mondini fifth in the Eurointernational #11, ahead of Graff’s #9, M. Racing’s #18 and Brundle’s United #2, which therefore started eighth in class.

chapters.title: Moineault under pressure
text: Moineault started the pole car but had two contacts, with Mondini’s #11 at Turn 3 on lap two and Rayhall’s Graff #10 at Turn 9 on lap 10, which earned a black-and-white flag. He ran third for 28 laps behind Brundle’s #2 and Droux’s #19, which led. Patterson lost six laps in the #3 after a puncture on lap three. At the first stops the #19 gave up the lead and Mondini took it, pulling away by nearly 30 seconds.

chapters.title: Leaders come and go
text: Eurointernational’s #11 and #12 lost their places in the second round of stops, and a full-course yellow for the stranded Villorba Corse #7 came around the half-way mark. M. Racing’s #18 led two hours in but lost seven minutes for rear bodywork repairs. Jacoboni then regained the lead in the #11 before contact at Turn 9 with two LMP2 cars ended its race on 105 laps. At the top of the third hour Duqueine led by 28 seconds from Graff’s #9, with the United #2 a further nine back.

chapters.title: The gap closes
text: The #19 stayed in front through the third round of stops, but the margin shrank. The #2 and the Graff #9 swapped places, and Kaiser took third for 360 Racing’s #6 from the Graff before the second full-course yellow. A third yellow in the last ten minutes, to recover Krohn’s LMP2 Ligier, tightened the field again.

chapters.title: Duqueine first on the road
text: Hallyday, Lunardi and Droux took the flag 3.5 seconds ahead of the United #2, with 360 Racing’s Woodward, Kaiser and Swift third. Hallyday said the team had done everything to avoid traps; Lunardi described a stint in which the car was almost undriveable. After the race the stewards gave the #19 a four-second penalty for breaching the minimum pit stop reference times. That put it behind the #2, and what had looked like a Duqueine win became United’s third.

chapters.title: Third win in three for the #2
text: The #2 won on 151 laps, with the penalised #19 second and 360 Racing’s #6 third, all on the same lap. Graff’s #9 was fourth and Oak’s #24 fifth, on 150 laps, ahead of Race Performance’s #8, Graff’s #10 and the pole-sitting #16 in eighth. Mondini set the class fastest lap, 1:26.829. Sixteen cars were classified; the #11, Ultimate’s #17 and Inter Europol’s #13, stopped after 42 laps, were not.
It was United’s third win from three races. The championship next heads to Paul Ricard.

LMGTE.title: JMW’s Ferrari leads and wins in LMGTE at the Red Bull Ring
LMGTE.dek: Smith, Butcher and Bertolini won for JMW’s Ferrari #66, a lap ahead of AF Corse, AT Racing and Aston Martin, after starting second to Cairoli’s Proton Porsche.

facts.v: The 20-year-old set 1:27.652 on his last of five laps to put the #88 Proton Porsche on pole by 0.121s.

one.label: Sportscar365: Double Pole for Panis Barthez at Red Bull Ring

facts.v: JMW’s Ferrari followed the Aston Martin at Silverstone and the Proton Porsche at Imola as the third different LMGTE winner in three rounds.

one.label: DailySportsCar: Red Bull Ring: TDS Oreca Takes The Win

facts.v: Butcher touched the Panis Barthez LMP2 Ligier on lap 27 and both ran off, but the JMW Ferrari carried on without significant damage.

chapters.title: Cairoli sets the pace
text: LMGTE arrived with no settled order. Aston Martin Racing’s #99 had won at Silverstone and Proton’s #77 at Imola, while JMW’s Ferrari #66, disqualified at Silverstone, was second at Imola. Eight cars were entered: four Ferrari 458s from AF Corse, AT Racing, JMW and Formula Racing, two Proton Porsches and a single Aston Martin.

Cairoli led from the start. His 1:28.824 in the #88 Porsche topped Friday’s practice, 0.240s ahead of Butcher’s JMW Ferrari, and on Saturday morning he went faster again, a 1:27.992 that left Pier Guidi’s AT Racing Ferrari 0.335s behind. Race Control also called several cars up for track-limits warnings in FP2, among them Formula Racing’s #60.

chapters.title: Cairoli completes the sweep
text: Cairoli took pole for Proton Competition with a 1:27.652 on the last of his five laps, and said the Ferraris were very close but that the team had managed its tyres well. Bertolini was second for JMW, 0.121s behind, and Pier Guidi third for AT Racing; those three were the only drivers under 1:28.
Cioci and Griffin were fourth and fifth in the AF Corse Ferraris, with Turner sixth for Aston Martin, Henzler seventh in the second Porsche and Mac eighth for Formula Racing.

chapters.title: Butcher takes the lead
text: Butcher passed the polesitting Porsche, started by Roda, in the opening laps and picked his way through the slower LMP3 cars. Scott, in AF Corse’s #55, tangled with an Oak LMP3 car but recovered to fifth in class. Seefried took the second Proton, the #77, to third within half an hour. On lap 27, while being lapped by the leading LMP2 car, Butcher touched the Panis Barthez Ligier and both ran off, but the Ferrari was able to carry on.

chapters.title: The lead changes hands
text: Butcher stayed in until the first scheduled stop and handed to Smith. Seefried did a second stint in the #77 and overtook the Talkanitsa Ferrari, and Smith then spun at Turn 1 when an LMP2 car passed around the outside, which gave Seefried the class lead. The full-course yellow near half-distance let most of the class make a scheduled stop. When the Porsche and the Aston Martin made theirs, Bertolini led with an hour and 45 minutes left, and Cairoli was second.

chapters.title: Ferraris move up
text: With an hour and 10 minutes to go Bertolini handed the JMW back to Butcher, and Cairoli stayed in the Porsche on the same lap. The final stops dropped the #88 to fifth in class. Aguas in the AF Corse #51 and Pier Guidi in the AT Racing #56 moved up to second and third, with MacDowall fourth in the Aston Martin.

chapters.title: An all-Ferrari podium
text: A full-course yellow in the last ten minutes, to recover Krohn’s beached LMP2 Ligier, changed nothing at the front. The JMW #66 won on 151 laps. The AF Corse #51 of Perazzini, Cioci and Aguas and the AT Racing #56 of the Talkanitsas and Pier Guidi were second and third, a lap down.

chapters.title: JMW’s first win of the year
text: The Aston Martin #99 was fourth and the Proton Porsche #88 fifth, both on 150 laps, with the other Proton, #77, sixth on 149 ahead of Formula Racing’s #60 and AF Corse’s #55. All eight cars were classified, and Cairoli set the class fastest lap, 1:29.166.
Bertolini said the key to being at the front was running without problems and respecting other drivers, and credited the team’s Bronze and Silver drivers. JMW had been disqualified at Silverstone.
